logistics.text: 35–45 min by taxi or metro + uphill bus/walk.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Strenuous (steep inclines, steps, gravel paths).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (exposed hillside, little shade in heat).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (transit + hill walk risks return buffer).

attractions.why: Perched on Carmel Hill, Gaudí's whimsical public park pairs colourful mosaic terraces and gingerbread-style gatehouses with sweeping views across the city to the sea.

attractions.name: Montserrat Monastery & Mountain

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 60–75 min each way by coach or train + rack railway.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate-Strenuous (steep mountain paths, stairs).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (mountain fog, wind, cooler temperatures).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (requires a dedicated 6–8 hr excursion).

attractions.why: Set high in a jagged, multi-peaked mountain range inland from Barcelona, this Benedictine abbey houses the revered Black Madonna and offers dramatic hiking trails.

shortDescription: Catalonia's vibrant seaside capital and a premier Mediterranean cruise hub, celebrated for Antoni Gaudí's fantastical Modernista architecture, lively La Rambla, Gothic Quarter alleys, and world-class tapas markets.
longDescription: Framed between the Mediterranean Sea and the Collserola hills, Barcelona effortlessly blends centuries-old Roman and medieval history with bold artistic innovation. Visitors can stand in awe beneath the soaring organic spires of Antoni Gaudí's Sagrada Família, stroll past mosaic lizards in Park Güell, admire the undulating stone facades of Casa Batlló and La Pedrera along Passeig de Gràcia, and wander the labyrinthine medieval lanes of the Barri Gòtic. Along the waterfront, the bustling La Boqueria market, Barceloneta beach promenade, and Montjuïc hilltop gardens offer endless culinary and cultural discoveries right beside one of Europe's busiest cruise ports.

tips.title: Know Your Terminal (Adossat vs. World Trade Center)
tips.text: Large cruise ships berth along the Moll Adossat breakwater (Terminals A, B, C, D, E, G, H), roughly 2–3 km from the Christopher Columbus Monument—use the paid Cruise Bus (Blue Bus) or a taxi rather than attempting the long bridge walk in summer heat. Smaller luxury vessels dock centrally at the World Trade Center piers right beside La Rambla.

tips.title: Book Gaudí Tickets Weeks in Advance
tips.text: Timed entry tickets for the Sagrada Família and Park Güell routinely sell out days or weeks ahead—reserve official online slots well before your sailing.

tips.title: Guard Against Pickpockets
tips.text: Barcelona is famously safe from violent crime, but pickpocketing is very common on La Rambla, inside La Boqueria, and on the Metro; use crossbody anti-theft bags and keep phones/wallets out of back pockets.

tips.title: Language & Dining Hours
tips.text: Both Catalan and Spanish are official languages, and locals eat late—traditional sit-down restaurants typically open for dinner around 8:30 PM, though tapas bars and cafes around El Born and Plaça Reial serve all afternoon.

stats.neighbours: Girona (historic medieval town, 40 minutes north via high-speed rail), Sitges (scenic coastal resort town, 40 minutes south), Montserrat (mountaintop monastery, 1 hour northwest).
stats.safety: Violent crime is exceptionally rare. However, Barcelona is internationally notorious for highly sophisticated pickpocketing networks, particularly on Las Ramblas and the Metro system. Keep personal items secure and close at all times.
stats.government: Governed as an autonomous community within the constitutional monarchy of Spain. While localized political tensions over Catalan independence can occasionally cause peaceful street demonstrations, the municipality is highly stable and secure.
stats.economy: Barcelona's regional economy generates a GDP of roughly €170B. Key economic pillars include tourism, logistics, automotive manufacturing, biomedical tech, and fashion.
stats.famousPeople: Antoni Gaudí (pioneering modernist architect), Joan Miró (surrealist painter), and contemporary sports icons like Gerard Piqué.
stats.vibe: Barcelona boasts an extraordinary architectural tapestry anchored by Gaudí’s surreal masterworks, including the unfinished basilica, La Sagrada Família.

timeline.text: Founded by the Romans as a military camp named Barcino.
Becomes a principal maritime and political seat for the Crown of Aragon.
Hosts the Summer Olympic Games, completely revitalizing the city's waterfront infrastructure and putting it on the modern tourism map.
Commemorates the centenary of Antoni Gaudí's death with major milestones in the final architectural phases of the Sagrada Família.

name: Belize City, Belize
area: Belize — Belize District; Belize Tourism Village.
currencyLanguage: BZD (USD widely accepted at BZ$2=US$1); English; Kriol and Spanish widely heard.
gettingAshore: Ships anchor offshore and tender 15–20 minutes to the Fort Street Tourism Village. Rough seas can delay or cancel tender operations. Almost all major natural and archaeological sights require substantial road or boat transfers. Confirm per call: tender boarding schedule, last tender time, and step-free tender capability.

attractions.name: Museum of Belize & St. John's Cathedral

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 10–15 min walk from Tourism Village.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (uneven city sidewalks, interior stairs at museum).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate (hot/humid; museum is air-conditioned).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Housed in a former 1857 colonial brick prison, the museum traces Maya history and Belizean heritage alongside Central America's oldest Anglican cathedral.

attractions.name: Altun Ha Maya Site

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 50–60 min drive north each way.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate (grassy plazas, steep stone temple steps).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (open sun, heat, humidity).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (allow 4.5–5 hours including tender).

attractions.why: The closest major ancient Maya ceremonial centre to Belize City, famous for its twin plazas and the Temple of the Masonry Altars where the giant Jade Head was discovered.

attractions.name: Nohoch Che'en Cave Tubing

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 60–70 min drive west each way.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate (30–40 min jungle walk carrying an inner tube; cool water).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (heavy rain raises river levels and closes caves).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (requires 5–6 hours).

attractions.why: Float on inner tubes through a subterranean limestone cave system illuminated by headlamps, drifting past crystalline stalactites and ancient Maya ceremonial ledges.

attractions.name: Belize Barrier Reef Snorkelling (Caye Caulker / Goff's Caye)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 30–45 min high-speed boat transfer from tender pier.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate (boat ladder boarding, open-water swimming).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (wind and swell directly affect boat comfort and visibility).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (requires 4.5–6 hours).

attractions.why: Part of the second-largest barrier reef system in the world, offering vibrant coral gardens, sea turtles, nurse sharks, and eagle rays in clear turquoise water.

attractions.name: Lamanai Archaeological Reserve

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 60 min road transfer + 45–60 min riverboat each way.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate-Strenuous (jungle trails, humid conditions, steep temple climbs).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (exposed boat ride and tropical rain/heat).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (strictly a 7–8 hour ship-sponsored excursion).

attractions.why: Combines a high-speed wildlife river safari up the New River Lagoon with towering jungle-shrouded Maya temples inhabited continuously for over 3,000 years.

shortDescription: A tender-only gateway to Central America's largest barrier reef, subterranean cave tubing rivers, and towering ancient Maya temple cities set deep in the tropical rainforest.
longDescription: Anchored offshore behind a protective string of coral cayes, Belize City serves as a springboard to some of the Caribbean's richest archaeological and ecological wonders. While the bustling coastal city itself features colonial landmarks like St. John's Cathedral and the historic Swing Bridge, most visitors head straight out toward Belize's interior jungles or offshore marine reserves. Adventures range from climbing the massive El Castillo pyramid at Xunantunich and exploring the ceremonial plazas of Altun Ha or Lamanai to floating on inner tubes through illuminated limestone river caves and snorkeling with nurse sharks and stingrays along the Belize Barrier Reef.

tips.title: Long Tender Rides
tips.text: Because shallow coastal waters prevent large ships from docking, expect a 15- to 20-minute high-speed tender ride each way to the Fort Street Tourism Village. Guests with ship-sponsored excursions typically receive priority tender tickets.

tips.title: Long Overland Drive Times
tips.text: Major Maya sites like Xunantunich and Lamanai involve 90-minute to 2-hour transfers each way; booking ship-sponsored tours is strongly recommended for distant inland excursions so the ship will wait in case of road delays.

tips.title: Stay Within Vetted Zones
tips.text: Downtown streets immediately outside the gated Fort Street Tourism Village can feel chaotic with aggressive street vendors; if exploring independently, arrange a licensed guide or official taxi at the terminal dispatch desk rather than wandering unescorted.

tips.title: Currency Simplicity
tips.text: The Belize Dollar (BZD) is pegged at a fixed 2:1 rate to the US Dollar (2 BZD = 1 USD), and USD cash is accepted everywhere—just expect change to be given in local Belizean notes and coins.

stats.population: ~68,000 (the largest city in the nation, though not the capital).
stats.landSize: 13 km² (city area); country size is 22,966 km².
stats.neighbours: Ladyville (home to the international airport), Caye Caulker and Ambergris Caye (accessible via water taxi), Belmopan (the capital city, 80 km inland).
stats.safety: The Tourism Village is highly secure. Certain neighborhoods in Belize City have high crime rates; travelers are advised to stick to pre-arranged shore excursions or official tourist zones.
stats.government: A highly stable parliamentary constitutional monarchy with King Charles III as the titular head of state. It boasts a peaceful democratic tradition.
stats.economy: GDP is roughly $3B. The economy relies heavily on tourism, agriculture (sugar, bananas, citrus fruits), and seafood exports.
stats.famousPeople: George Cadle Price (the "Father of the Nation"), Shyne Barrow (rapper turned politician), and Simone Biles (the legendary gymnast, who holds dual Belizean-American citizenship).
stats.vibe: Belize is the only country in Central America where English is the official language. The culture is a vibrant blend of Maya, Garifuna, Creole, and Mestizo traditions.

timeline.text: The classic Maya Civilization flourishes across inland Belize.
English buccaneers (pirates) establish Belize City as a logging settlement.
The Battle of St. George's Caye: British settlers definitively defeat a Spanish fleet.
Belize gains full independence from Great Britain (formerly known as British Honduras).

name: Benoa (Bali)
currencyLanguage: IDR (cards accepted at hotels/restaurants; IDR cash needed for temple donations, markets, and local drivers); Indonesian and Balinese (English widely spoken in tourist areas).
gettingAshore: Cruise ships dock at the Bali Maritime Tourism Hub (BMTH) / Benoa Cruise Terminal along a narrow peninsula connecting Sanur, Nusa Dua, and Kuta. Traffic in southern Bali is notoriously heavy and unpredictable; allow generous return buffers. Pre-booked private drivers, vetted port taxis, or ship excursions are strongly recommended. Confirm per call: BMTH terminal berth, port gate taxi pickup rules, and temple dress-code sarong requirements.

attractions.name: Uluwatu Cliff Temple (Pura Luhur Uluwatu) & Nusa Dua Waterblow
attractions.tier: Local Transit / Independent or Guided Excursion

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 45–60 min drive southwest to Uluwatu (25 min to Nusa Dua), subject to heavy traffic.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate (cliffside stone walkways and steps; watch belongings around mischievous macaques).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (exposed 70m limestone ocean cliffs; hot tropical sun).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Borderline (allow 4.5–5 hours for Uluwatu; Nusa Dua easily fits in 3 hours).

attractions.why: Perched dramatically atop a sheer 70-metre sea cliff above crashing Indian Ocean surf, showcasing classic Balinese coral-stone temple gates and sweeping coastal views.

attractions.name: Sanur Beachfront Promenade & Bajra Sandhi Monument (Denpasar)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 20–25 min taxi north along the Bali Mandara Toll Road.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (flat paved beachfront boardwalk and park paths).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate (warm tropical coast; shaded beachside cafes).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Offers a relaxed, walkable seaside promenade lined with traditional colourful jukung outrigger boats, beach cafes, and a grand monument celebrating Balinese history.

attractions.name: Tanah Lot Sea Temple

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 60–90 min drive northwest through Denpasar traffic each way.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate (paved market approach, uneven rocky coastal steps at low tide).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (exposed Indian Ocean rock outcrop).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (allow 5–6 hours due to traffic).

attractions.why: Bali's most iconic offshore Hindu sea temple perched atop a wave-carved rock formation just off the southwestern coast.

attractions.name: Ubud Cultural Heartland (Tegallalang Rice Terraces, Sacred Monkey Forest & Ubud Palace)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 75–105 min drive north inland each way depending on traffic.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate-Strenuous (steep terraced paths, uneven forest steps, humid jungle air).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate-High (tropical heat/humidity and afternoon rain showers).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (strictly a 7–8.5 hour full-day excursion).

attractions.why: Explores Bali's artistic and spiritual interior, combining emerald-green tiered rice paddies, traditional woodcarving villages, and lush temple groves.

shortDescription: The maritime gateway to Indonesia's "Island of the Gods," connecting cruise travelers to cliffside sea temples like Uluwatu and Tanah Lot, Ubud's emerald rice terraces, traditional Balinese dance, and Nusa Dua beaches.
longDescription: Positioned on a narrow peninsula in southern Bali just minutes from Nusa Dua and Kuta, Benoa Harbour opens the door to Bali's deeply spiritual Hindu culture and lush tropical landscapes. Travelers can venture inland to the artistic highland town of Ubud to stroll beneath towering banyan trees in the Sacred Monkey Forest, admire the stepped emerald paddies of Tegalalang, and browse woodcarving villages, or hug the dramatic southern limestone cliffs to watch Kecak fire dances at Uluwatu Temple and explore water-surrounded Tanah Lot. Closer to the pier, sandy Nusa Dua and Sanur beaches offer relaxed coastal resorts and water sports.

tips.title: Heavy Bali Traffic & Drive Times
tips.text: Bali's narrow two-lane roads suffer notorious traffic congestion; reaching Ubud (~90–120 minutes each way) or Tanah Lot (~75–90 minutes each way) consumes much of the day—book ship-sponsored excursions or leave at least a 90-minute return buffer if hiring a private driver.

tips.title: Temple Dress Code (Sarong & Sash)
tips.text: Modest attire is strictly enforced at all Balinese Hindu temples; shoulders and knees must be covered, and visitors must wear a traditional sarong and waist sash (usually provided free or for a small rental fee at temple entrances).

tips.title: Indonesia Visa & Tourist Levy
tips.text: Verify current Indonesian Visa on Arrival (VOA) and Bali Provincial Tourist Levy rules prior to sailing (many cruise lines facilitate transit entry for port calls, while turnaround guests must complete online declarations).

tips.title: Currency, Water & Monkey Etiquette
tips.text: The Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) is the official currency (USD is accepted by major tour operators, though IDR cash is needed for small shops and temple donations); drink only sealed bottled water, and secure sunglasses, hats, and phones tightly around macaques at Uluwatu and Ubud Monkey Forest.

stats.intro: Benoa is the principal maritime cruise gateway to Bali—the world-famous "Island of the Gods"—where rich Hindu culture, volcanic landscapes, and terraced rice paddies meet.
stats.neighbours: Ubud (the cultural and artistic heart of Bali, nestled among lush rainforests and rice terraces, 1 hour 15 minutes north), Uluwatu Temple (a majestic sea temple perched precariously on a sheer cliff face, 40 minutes southwest).
stats.safety: Generally very safe and welcoming, with a deeply hospitable local culture. The primary travel concerns are petty opportunism (like pickpocketing in crowded markets) and transit safety—traffic can be chaotic, so hiring an official licensed driver is highly recommended.
stats.government: Stable provincial government operating as a special tourism and cultural zone within the democratic Republic of Indonesia.
stats.economy: Heavily driven by international leisure and cultural tourism, traditional arts and crafts exporting, seaweed farming, high-yield agriculture, and marine cargo logistics.
stats.famousPeople: I Gusti Ngurah Rai (celebrated national hero and revolutionary leader), and generations of master woodcarvers and stone sculptors.
stats.vibe: Deeply spiritual, artistic, and relaxed. The island’s unique form of Balinese Hinduism influences daily life, from the intricate palm-leaf canang sari flower offerings on every doorstep to the hypnotic Kecak fire dances. The culinary signature is Babi Guling (spit-roasted suckling pig seasoned with local spices).

timeline.text: The powerful Majapahit Empire from Java establishes a major presence on Bali, deeply influencing its architecture, religion, and courtly arts.
Dutch colonial forces launch a military intervention in South Bali, leading to the tragic Puputan mass suicide of the local royal courts who refused surrender.
Bali implements its innovative, sustainable tourism levy program to directly fund the preservation of the island's unique coral reefs, forests, and ancient temples.

name: Bergen
currencyLanguage: NOK (cards accepted everywhere); Norwegian (English widely spoken).
gettingAshore: Ships berth primarily at Skolten / Bontelabo (a flat 10–15 minute waterfront walk past Bergenhus Fortress to Bryggen) or across the peninsula at Dokken / Jekteviken (25–30 minute walk or 10-minute port shuttle to the city centre). Confirm per call: assigned terminal (Skolten/Bontelabo vs. Dokken/Jekteviken), shuttle pickup, and Fløibanen funicular timed tickets.

attractions.name: Bryggen Hanseatic Wharf & Bergenhus Fortress

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 5–15 min flat walk from Skolten/Bontelabo (or 10 min shuttle from Dokken).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (uneven historic wooden planks and narrow alleys in Bryggen).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate (Bergen averages over 200 rainy days annually; bring rain gear).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: A UNESCO World Heritage site of colourful leaning timber merchant houses dating back to the 14th-century Hanseatic League, now housing artisan studios and maritime museums.

attractions.name: Fløibanen Funicular & Mount Fløyen

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 15–20 min walk from Skolten to lower station + 6 min funicular ride.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (step-free funicular carriages; paved summit terrace and forest trails).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (summit views often shrouded in mist; pre-book tickets to skip queues).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Climbs 320 metres above Bergen in minutes to panoramic terraces overlooking the city's seven mountains, harbour, and surrounding coastal islands.

attractions.name: Bergen Fish Market (Fisketorget) & KODE Art Museums

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 15–20 min flat walk from Skolten along Vågen harbour.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (flat harbourfront promenades and accessible museum galleries).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Low (indoor Mathallen food hall and museum buildings).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Sample fresh king crab, smoked salmon, and fish soup at the harbourfront market before browsing Edvard Munch masterpieces at the KODE galleries beside Lille Lungegårdsvannet lake.

attractions.name: Mostraumen Fjord Cruise

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 15–20 min walk to Zachariasbryggen / Strandkaien departure quay (3.5 hr round-trip boat).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (seated sightseeing catamaran with outdoor decks).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate (heated indoor lounge with panoramic windows).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Borderline (only suitable for 5+ hr port calls).

attractions.why: Sails directly from Bergen's harbour through narrow, steep-walled Osterfjord and the powerful Mostraumen tidal current right up to cascading mountain waterfalls.

shortDescription: Norway's historic Hanseatic trading port nestled among seven mountains, famous for the UNESCO-listed wooden wharf of Bryggen, the Fløibanen funicular, lively fish markets, and scenic fjord cruises.
longDescription: Surrounded by seven steep mountains and island-dotted fjords, Bergen blends centuries of maritime merchant heritage with vibrant Norwegian coastal culture. Steps from the harbourfront stands Bryggen—a UNESCO World Heritage row of crooked, ochre-and-red timber warehouses dating back to the 14th-century Hanseatic League—alongside Bergenhus Fortress and the bustling Fish Market (Fisketorget). Above the city, the Fløibanen funicular climbs 320 metres in six minutes to Mount Fløyen's panoramic terraces and forest trails, while harbour catamarans sail directly from the waterfront into narrow, waterfall-laced Mostraumen fjord.

tips.title: Berth Location (Skolten/Bontelabo vs. Dokken/Jekteviken)
tips.text: Ships docking at Skolten or Bontelabo enjoy a flat 10- to 15-minute walk past Bergenhus Fortress straight into Bryggen; ships berthed across the peninsula at Dokken or Jekteviken require a 25- to 30-minute walk or a 10-minute port shuttle into the centre.

tips.title: Pre-Book Fløibanen Funicular Tickets
tips.text: On multi-ship days, ticket-office lines at the Fløibanen lower station can exceed 45–60 minutes—buy timed tickets online via the Fløibanen app or website to walk straight into the boarding queue.

tips.title: Pack Rain Gear Year-Round
tips.text: Known as Europe's rainiest city (averaging over 200 rainy days per year), Bergen can shift from sunshine to steady drizzle in minutes—always carry a waterproof rain jacket and non-slip shoes for wet wooden planks in Bryggen.

tips.title: Mostraumen Fjord Boat Timing
tips.text: The popular 3.5-hour Mostraumen Fjord Cruise departs right from Zachariasbryggen in the inner harbour; verify departure times carefully so you have at least 45 minutes of buffer before all-aboard.

stats.neighbours: Fløyen & Ulriken (two of the seven iconic mountains surrounding the city, accessible via funicular and cable car directly from downtown), Hardangerfjord (spectacular fjord landscape, 1.5 hours east).
stats.safety: Highly secure. Normal, standard big-city awareness is recommended around the high-density Fish Market (Fisketorget) and Bryggen wharf area where pickpockets may occasionally browse cruise crowds.
stats.government: Major historic municipal capital within Norway, boasting immense institutional stability.
stats.economy: A multi-billion dollar economic hub fueled by offshore oil and gas maritime tech, aquaculture (salmon farming), commercial shipping networks, and high-volume international tourism.
stats.famousPeople: Edvard Grieg (legendary romantic-era classical composer), Kygo (world-famous contemporary electronic music producer), and Ole Bull (celebrated violin virtuoso).
stats.vibe: Famous for Bryggen—the UNESCO-listed row of leaning, historic wooden merchant houses. It is also known as one of the wettest cities in Europe, with locals embracing the cozy rainy vibe in style.

timeline.text: Founded by King Olav Kyrre, quickly rising to become Norway's first royal capital city.
The Hanseatic League establishes a principal trading post (Kontor) in Bergen, monopolizing the lucrative stockfish trade for centuries.
The historic merchant houses of Bryggen are formally inscribed onto the UNESCO World Heritage list, ensuring their preservation.

name: Bilbao
currencyLanguage: EUR; Basque and Spanish.
gettingAshore: Cruise ships berth at the Olatua Cruise Terminal in Getxo, located roughly 15 km northwest of central Bilbao at the mouth of the Nervión estuary. Walking to central Bilbao is not possible; use the cruise shuttle bus, taxi (20–25 min), or the Bilbao Metro (Neguri or Gobela stations are a 15–20 min walk from the terminal; 25 min ride into central Bilbao). Confirm per call: terminal berth, shuttle drop-off location in Bilbao, and metro lift access.

attractions.name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 20–25 min shuttle/taxi from Getxo terminal (or 45 min walk + metro).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (fully accessible, modern ramps and elevators).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: None (indoor museum; riverside sculptures outdoors).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Frank Gehry's titanium-clad architectural masterpiece along the Nervión River, showcasing monumental contemporary art installations and Jeff Koons' floral Puppy.

attractions.name: Casco Viejo (Seven Streets) & Ribera Market

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 25–30 min taxi/metro from Getxo (or 20 min riverside walk from Guggenheim).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (flat pedestrianized streets, busy pintxos bars).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Low (covered market hall and narrow lanes).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Bilbao's medieval core, celebrated for Plaza Nueva, Santiago Cathedral, Europe's largest covered Art Deco food market, and world-class Basque pintxos hopping.

attractions.name: Vizcaya Bridge (Puente Colgante) & Getxo Waterfront
attractions.tier: Walk-Off / Independent (long walk) or Local Transit

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 5–10 min taxi from Getxo cruise terminal (or 35 min flat seaside promenade walk).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (gondola transporter is step-free; upper walkway requires elevator).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate (exposed estuary bridge).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and the world's oldest surviving transporter bridge (1893), carrying passengers and cars across the estuary in a suspended gondola.

attractions.name: San Juan de Gaztelugatxe & Guernica

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 45–60 min drive each way along winding coastal/rural roads.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Strenuous (Gaztelugatxe involves a steep 241-step stone bridge climb; timed entry permit required).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (steep coastal steps close in severe wind/rain).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (requires 6–7+ hours).

attractions.why: Pairs a dramatic wave-lashed islet hermitage on the Basque coast with the historic town of Guernica, symbol of Basque heritage and Picasso's famous anti-war painting.

shortDescription: The vibrant cultural capital of Spain's Basque Country, world-famous for Frank Gehry's titanium-clad Guggenheim Museum, the historic Vizcaya Transporter Bridge, and world-class pintxos gastronomy.
longDescription: Transformed from an industrial river port into a global showcase of contemporary architecture and culinary excellence, Bilbao straddles the Nervión River amidst lush green Basque hills. Visitors can marvel at the shimmering titanium curves of the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao and Jeff Koons' giant floral Puppy, ride the 1893 UNESCO-listed Vizcaya Transporter Bridge across the estuary near the cruise terminal, and wander the medieval Seven Streets of Casco Viejo to sample artistic Basque pintxos alongside Ribera Market. Further along the rugged coast lie the dramatic wave-lashed hermitage of San Juan de Gaztelugatxe and the historic town of Guernica.

tips.title: Berth Location in Getxo (15 km from Central Bilbao)
tips.text: Cruise ships dock at the Olatua Cruise Terminal in Getxo at the mouth of the estuary, not in downtown Bilbao—use the cruise shuttle bus, a 20–25 minute taxi, or walk 15–20 minutes to Neguri / Gobela Metro stations for a 25-minute ride into central Bilbao.

tips.title: Guggenheim Museum Planning
tips.text: Closed on most Mondays outside peak summer months—verify opening days and pre-book timed tickets online; audio guides are included with admission.

tips.title: Vizcaya Bridge Right Beside Getxo
tips.text: The historic Puente Colgante (Vizcaya Bridge) sits just a 5–10 minute taxi ride (or 35-minute flat waterfront promenade walk) from the Getxo cruise terminal, making it an easy add-on before or after central Bilbao.

tips.title: Gaztelugatxe Permits & Steps
tips.text: Visiting San Juan de Gaztelugatxe requires a steep 241-step stone causeway climb and free timed-entry reservations during peak seasons—only attempt on 6.5+ hour port calls.

stats.neighbours: San Sebastián (culinary resort capital, 1 hour east), Guernica (historic Basque capital, 35 minutes east), Getxo (coastal town where cruise ships berth at the outer port, 20 minutes north via metro).
stats.safety: Very safe. Standard, common-sense big-city awareness is all that is required, especially on public transit or around crowded museum plazas where petty pickpockets might operate.
stats.government: Capital of the Biscay province in the stable, highly autonomous Basque Country of Spain.
stats.economy: Dominated by a highly modernized economy spanning metallurgy, maritime logistics, engineering, banking, and high-tier cultural tourism.
stats.famousPeople: Miguel de Unamuno (influential essayist and novelist), and historic Basque navigators.
stats.vibe: The city is the epicentre of Basque gastronomy, famous for Pintxos (gourmet small plates served on skewers) and its unique, non-Indo-European Basque language (Euskera).

timeline.text: Founded by Diego López V de Haro, evolving into a critical commercial iron-trade gateway.
Suffers a severe economic decline as traditional steel and shipbuilding industries collapse.
The opening of the Frank Gehry-designed titanium Guggenheim Museum triggers the "Bilbao Effect," completely revitalizing the city into a global cultural landmark.

name: Bordeaux (Le Verdon)
currencyLanguage: EUR; French.
gettingAshore: Large ocean cruise ships typically berth at Le Verdon-sur-Mer at the mouth of the Gironde estuary, roughly 90 km (75–90 minutes by road) northwest of central Bordeaux, while smaller ships may sail upriver to dock directly at Port de la Lune in downtown Bordeaux. Never assume central docking without confirming the call's berth. Confirm per call: berth location (Le Verdon vs. downtown Bordeaux), cruise shuttle schedule, and train/coach transfer times.

attractions.name: Place de la Bourse, Miroir d'Eau & Port de la Lune (UNESCO)
attractions.tier: Walk-Off / Independent (if docked in city) or Full-Day Excursion (from Le Verdon)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 5–10 min walk from downtown berths; 75–90 min coach/transfer from Le Verdon.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (flat riverside esplanade and limestone squares).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Low-Moderate.

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes (only if docked in downtown Bordeaux); No (from Le Verdon).

attractions.why: Bordeaux's iconic 18th-century neoclassical riverfront ensemble fronted by the world's largest reflecting pool (Miroir d'Eau) and grand pedestrian avenues.

attractions.name: La Cité du Vin
attractions.tier: Local Transit / Independent (from city berths) or Full-Day Excursion (from Le Verdon)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 15 min Tram B ride from downtown Bordeaux (or 80 min coach from Le Verdon).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (modern, fully step-free museum with elevators).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: None (fully indoor interactive museum).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes (if docked in city); No (from Le Verdon).

attractions.why: A striking decanter-shaped cultural museum exploring global wine history, sensory exhibits, and culminating in a panoramic tasting on the 8th-floor Belvedere.

attractions.name: Médoc Wine Route & Classified Châteaux (Pauillac / Margaux)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 45–60 min coach south from Le Verdon (or 45 min north from downtown Bordeaux).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (gravel courtyard paths, cellar stairs).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Low (indoor cellar tastings).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (allow 5–7 hours for estate tours and tastings).

attractions.why: Winds through legendary Left Bank Cabernet Sauvignon vineyards to visit historic grand cru châteaux, barrel rooms, and tutored tastings.

attractions.name: Soulac-sur-Mer & Cordouan Lighthouse Viewpoint

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 15 min taxi or local train south from Le Verdon terminal.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (flat seaside resort streets and sandy beach).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate (exposed Atlantic coast).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes (ideal short-call alternative when docked at Le Verdon).

attractions.why: A charming Belle Époque seaside resort near Le Verdon featuring 19th-century villas, a UNESCO-listed basilica, and views toward France's oldest lighthouse.

shortDescription: France's world-famous wine capital along the Garonne River, offering grand 18th-century neoclassical architecture, the interactive Cité du Vin museum, and legendary Médoc and Saint-Émilion vineyard châteaux.
longDescription: Celebrated globally as the heartland of fine French winemaking, Bordeaux combines sweeping 18th-century stone boulevards with prestigious surrounding appellations. Depending on ship size, vessels either sail directly up the Garonne River to berth in central Bordeaux steps from Place de la Bourse and its famed Water Mirror, or dock at the coastal deep-water terminal of Le Verdon-sur-Mer at the mouth of the Gironde estuary. From either berth, travelers can explore the interactive wine-culture exhibits at La Cité du Vin, stroll pedestrianized Rue Sainte-Catherine, or tour historic gravel-soil wine estates in Pauillac, Margaux, and medieval Saint-Émilion.

tips.title: Know Your Berth (Central Bordeaux vs. Le Verdon-sur-Mer)
tips.text: Smaller and mid-sized ships dock right in Port de la Lune in downtown Bordeaux (walk-off access to trams and Place de la Bourse), whereas large ocean liners berth at Le Verdon-sur-Mer, roughly 90 to 105 minutes north of central Bordeaux by coach or regional train—always verify which port your ship uses before booking independent plans.

tips.title: Château Tasting Reservations
tips.text: Prestigious Médoc and Saint-Émilion wine estates require advance appointments for cellar tours and tastings; ship-sponsored wine excursions or pre-booked private drivers are the easiest way to visit multiple châteaux seamlessly.

tips.title: Book La Cité du Vin Early
tips.text: If visiting La Cité du Vin in Bordeaux's Bassins à Flot district (reachable via Tram B), reserve timed entry tickets online ahead of time; admission includes a complimentary glass of wine at the 8th-floor Belvedere overlooking the city.

tips.title: Try Local Canelés
tips.text: Don't leave Bordeaux without tasting a warm canelé—the city's signature caramelized, rum-and-vanilla fluted pastry from iconic local bakeries like Baillardran.

stats.population: ~1,300 (Le Verdon-sur-Mer proper), providing access to Bordeaux's metropolitan population of ~820,000.
stats.neighbours: Bordeaux Center (world wine capital, approx. 100 km south, reachable via scenic regional train or cruise tour coach in about 1.5 to 2 hours), Soulac-sur-Mer (charming 19th-century seaside resort town, 10 minutes south).
stats.safety: Le Verdon is an exceptionally quiet, rural, and safe maritime community. If you take an excursion or train south into central Bordeaux, maintain standard big-city vigilance against pickpockets around high-frequency tramway stations and busy public plazas like Place de la Bourse.
stats.government: Highly stable French municipal structure within the Gironde department and the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region.
stats.economy: Le Verdon relies heavily on deep-water timber and container logistics, holiday tourism, and oyster cultivation. The wider Bordeaux region is a global economic powerhouse driven by premium wine production, aerospace engineering, tourism, and digital technology.
stats.famousPeople: Celebrated historic wine barons of the Médoc peninsula, and prominent French philosophers like Michel de Montaigne and Montesquieu who lived and wrote in the wider region.
stats.vibe: Positioned at the northern tip of the famous Médoc wine peninsula, this port gives travelers direct access to some of the world's most prestigious vineyards, châteaux, and traditional French oyster shacks.

timeline.text: The Cordouan Lighthouse, standing just offshore from Le Verdon, undergoes major renovations; it is the oldest continuous operating lighthouse in France (built 1611) and a UNESCO landmark.
Le Verdon serves as a critical strategic landing base for the American Expeditionary Forces arriving in Europe during World War I.
The deep-water mole and modern outer port infrastructure are officially inaugurated to handle large ocean liners that cannot navigate up-river to Bordeaux.

name: Brisbane
currencyLanguage: AUD (contactless cards and mobile tap accepted virtually everywhere); English.

officialLinks.label: Port of Brisbane — Brisbane International Cruise Terminal

gettingAshore: Most large ocean cruise ships berth at the Brisbane International Cruise Terminal (BICT) at Luggage Point on the mouth of the Brisbane River, roughly 20 km (25–35 minutes by taxi/rideshare or cruise shuttle) northeast of the Brisbane CBD; there is no public train/ferry station directly at BICT. Smaller vessels occasionally sail upriver to dock at Portside Wharf in Hamilton (20 minutes by CityCat river ferry to downtown). Confirm per call: BICT vs. Portside Wharf berth, cruise shuttle drop-off at Eagle Street Pier/CBD, and Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary riverboat schedule.

attractions.name: South Bank Parklands, Streets Beach & Queensland Art Gallery / GOMA

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 25–35 min taxi/rideshare or cruise shuttle from BICT to CBD + 10 min walk across Victoria Bridge.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (flat riverside promenades, shaded arbour walkways, and accessible museum galleries).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (air-conditioned art galleries; sunny subtropical riverfront).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Brisbane's vibrant cultural riverfront featuring a man-made lagoon beach, bougainvillea-draped walkways, and Australia's premier modern art museum (GOMA).

attractions.name: Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary
attractions.tier: Local Transit / Independent or Guided Excursion

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 35–45 min taxi/rideshare from BICT (or 75 min scenic Mirimar river cruise from South Bank).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (paved shaded eucalyptus sanctuary paths with gentle slopes).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate (shaded outdoor wildlife enclosures).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes (via direct taxi/shuttle; river cruise requires 5+ hrs).

attractions.why: The world's first and largest koala sanctuary, offering close-up encounters with koalas, hand-feeding free-roaming kangaroos, and platypus viewing.

attractions.name: CityCat River Ferry, Howard Smith Wharves & Story Bridge

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 25–30 min taxi/shuttle from BICT to Howard Smith Wharves / Eagle Street Pier.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (flat riverfront boardwalks and accessible catamaran ferries).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (covered ferry cabins and open decks).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Cruise along the winding Brisbane River beneath the iconic steel Story Bridge, stopping at lively riverside craft breweries and dining pavilions tucked beneath the cliffs.

attractions.name: Australia Zoo (Sunshine Coast) or Gold Coast (Surfers Paradise)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 60–75 min drive north to Australia Zoo or 60–75 min drive south to Gold Coast each way.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate (expansive zoo parklands or sandy surf beaches).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (warm Queensland sun and humidity).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (strictly a 6–8 hour full-day excursion).

attractions.why: Visits either Steve Irwin's world-famous wildlife conservation zoo on the Sunshine Coast or the golden surf beaches and skyline of the Gold Coast.

shortDescription: Queensland's sunny, subtropical river capital, offering koala encounters at Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary, lush South Bank parklands, Moreton Island dolphin cruises, and gateway access to the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast.
longDescription: Winding along the Brisbane River beneath year-round blue skies, Brisbane pairs laid-back Australian outdoor lifestyle with vibrant cultural districts and world-famous wildlife experiences. Depending on ship size, guests arrive at the modern Brisbane International Cruise Terminal at Luggage Point or closer upriver at Hamilton, with easy access to the riverside boardwalks, galleries, and man-made lagoon beach of South Bank. Nature lovers can cuddle or spot koalas and hand-feed kangaroos at Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary, climb the Story Bridge for panoramic skyline views, or take a fast catamaran to Moreton Island's Tangalooma wrecks.

tips.title: Know Your Cruise Terminal (BICT vs. Portside Wharf)
tips.text: Nearly all large cruise ships dock at the Brisbane International Cruise Terminal (BICT) at Luggage Point near the mouth of the river (~20 km / 25–30 minutes east of downtown by cruise shuttle, taxi, or Uber—there is no train station or walkable town outside BICT). Smaller luxury ships occasionally berth upriver at Portside Wharf (Hamilton), which connects directly to downtown via Brisbane's scenic CityCat river ferries.

tips.title: Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary River Cruise & Booking
tips.text: Located ~25 minutes southwest of downtown, Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary can be reached by taxi/Uber, public bus, or a scenic Mirimar Cruises river boat from South Bank; book koala encounter experiences and entry tickets online ahead of time.

tips.title: High Australian UV & Subtropical Heat
tips.text: Brisbane enjoys strong year-round sunshine; pack high-SPF sunscreen, sunglasses, a wide-brimmed hat, and lightweight breathable clothing, especially from November through March.

tips.title: Cashless Convenience & Biosecurity Rules
tips.text: Australia is virtually cashless (contactless Visa/Mastercard and Apple/Google Pay work everywhere in AUD); remember Australia enforces strict biosecurity laws prohibiting carrying fresh fruit, nuts, honey, or unsealed snacks off the ship.

stats.intro: Brisbane is a sun-drenched, sophisticated river city that seamlessly pairs a relaxed, outdoor lifestyle with cutting-edge urban art precincts and direct access to world-famous surf coasts.
stats.neighbours: The Gold Coast (famous for world-class surf breaks and theme parks, 1 hour south), The Sunshine Coast (pristine beaches and sub-tropical hinterland villages, 1 hour north), Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary (located right within the city outskirts).
stats.safety: Very safe, clean, and highly accessible. Standard big-city awareness is recommended at night around major entertainment hubs like Fortitude Valley, but street crime is exceptionally low.
stats.government: Stable political capital of the state of Queensland, operating under Australia's secure democratic framework.
stats.economy: A booming multi-billion-dollar economy driven by international education, mineral and agricultural trade shipping, information technology, green energy infrastructure, and high-volume cruise tourism.
stats.famousPeople: The Bee Gees (pop music legends who began their career nearby), Bluey (the globally adored animated character whose show is set entirely in Brisbane), Margot Robbie (Academy Award-nominated actress from the region).
stats.vibe: Laid-back, warm, and highly active. The heart of the city centers on South Bank, featuring Australia's only inner-city, man-made sandy beach. Locals love the craft brewery scene, riverside dining, and outdoor active lifestyle. The local culinary signature highlights fresh Moreton Bay Bugs (a delicious local flathead lobster).

timeline.text: Established as a harsh penal colony for repeat British convicts at Redcliffe before moving to the current Brisbane River site.
Serves as the high-profile South West Pacific headquarters for US General Douglas MacArthur during World War II.
Hosts World Expo 88, permanently transforming the industrial south bank into the magnificent cultural parklands seen today.

name: Broome
currencyLanguage: AUD (cards widely accepted; carry small AUD cash for Courthouse Markets and local buses); English.

officialLinks.label: Kimberley Ports Authority — Port of Broome

gettingAshore: Cruise ships berth at Broome Deepwater Jetty at Entrance Point, roughly 7 km south of Chinatown and 10 km from Cable Beach. Broome experiences extreme tidal ranges (up to 9–10 metres), which can result in very steep gangways at low tide. Complimentary cruise shuttles or local town buses connect the jetty to Chinatown (10–15 minutes). Confirm per call: gangway tidal slope/accessibility, shuttle drop-off in Chinatown, and tide times for Gantheaume Point dinosaur footprints.

attractions.name: Cable Beach

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 15–20 min taxi or Broome Explorer Bus from Chinatown shuttle drop-off.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (paved beachfront promenade; soft white sand down to water).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (intense tropical Kimberley sun and heat; seasonal marine stingers Nov–May).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Twenty-two kilometres of pristine white sand meeting turquoise Indian Ocean waters, famous for dramatic red ochre cliffs and iconic beachfront camel walks.

attractions.name: Chinatown Pearling Heritage Precinct & Sun Pictures

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 10–15 min port shuttle bus from Broome Jetty.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (flat heritage streets and shaded wooden walkways).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (air-conditioned pearl showrooms and historic open-air cinema).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Explores Broome's multicultural South Sea pearl-diving history through restored corrugated-iron lugger sheds, Australian South Sea pearl galleries, and the world's oldest operating open-air picture gardens (1916).

attractions.name: Gantheaume Point & Anastasia's Pool
attractions.tier: Local Transit / Independent or Guided Excursion

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 10–15 min taxi west from Broome Jetty (located near the southern tip of Cable Beach).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate (uneven red pindan sandstone ledges; tidal rock pools).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (exposed red-rock headland; dinosaur footprints visible only at very low tide).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Striking red-ochre sandstone cliffs contrasting with vivid turquoise water, featuring plaster casts of 130-million-year-old dinosaur tracks and dramatic coastal scenery.

attractions.name: Malcolm Douglas Crocodile Park & Roebuck Bay Hovercraft / Eco-Cruise

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 15–20 min drive east/north depending on tour.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (flat shaded wildlife park paths or seated hovercraft/boat tour).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (tropical heat and humidity).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes (2.5–3.5 hr tours available).

attractions.why: Features massive saltwater crocodiles during daily feeding shows or skims across Roebuck Bay's vibrant red mudflats and mangroves.

shortDescription: A remote, sun-drenched pearling town on Western Australia's Kimberley coast, famed for iconic camel rides along 22-kilometre Cable Beach, turquoise-and-red pindan cliffs, dinosaur footprints, and South Sea pearl farms.
longDescription: Perched between the rust-red Outback of the Kimberley and the dazzling turquoise waters of the Indian Ocean, Broome charms visitors with its storied 19th-century pearling heritage and dramatic natural contrasts. Ships dock at the deep-water Port of Broome jetty at Entrance Point, minutes from the red ochre cliffs and dinosaur footprints of Gantheaume Point, historic Chinatown's pearl showrooms, and the sweeping white sands of Cable Beach—where sunset camel trains silhouette against glowing Indian Ocean skies.

tips.title: Port Shuttle & Extreme Tidal Swings
tips.text: Broome experiences massive 9- to 10-metre tidal swings that create steep gangway angles at Broome Wharf; because the wharf sits ~7 km south of Chinatown and ~10 km from Cable Beach with no public transit at the gate, use the cruise shuttle bus, local Broome Explorer Bus, or pre-booked tour transport.

tips.title: Marine Stinger Season (November–May)
tips.text: Box jellyfish and Irukandji stingers inhabit Kimberley coastal waters during the wet season (roughly November through May)—swim only inside patrolled stinger nets if open, and heed local beach warning flags.

tips.title: Check Tide Tables for Gantheaume Point & Staircase to the Moon
tips.text: Fossilized 130-million-year-old dinosaur footprints at Gantheaume Point are only visible at very low tide (casts are displayed at the top of the cliffs at high tide); if calling during an evening full moon between March and October, watch for the optical illusion known as the Staircase to the Moon across Roebuck Bay mudflats.

tips.title: Book Cable Beach Camel Rides & Pearl Farm Tours Early
tips.text: Broome is an isolated Outback town with limited tour capacity—reserve Cable Beach camel rides, Willie Creek Pearl Farm tours, or Horizontal Falls scenic flights well before your sailing.

stats.intro: Broome is a dramatic, wild frontier town where the fiery red sands of the Kimberley outback crash directly into the turquoise waters of the Indian Ocean—a region legendary for its rich pearl-diving history.
stats.neighbours: The Kimberley Wilderness (one of the world's last great pristine wilderness frontiers, stretching north), Cable Beach (a breathtaking, 22-kilometer stretch of pure white sand, 10 minutes west).
stats.safety: Generally safe with a relaxed, small-town atmosphere. The primary travel warnings are environmental: the tides here are massive and fast-moving (up to 10 meters), and travelers should pay close attention to seasonal warnings regarding marine stingers or estuarine crocodiles.
stats.government: Structured local governance under the Shire of Broome within Western Australia.
stats.economy: Heavily driven by premium South Sea pearl aquaculture, beef exporting, offshore oil and gas logistics, and high-end seasonal outback adventure tourism.
stats.famousPeople: Master pearl divers of Japanese, Malay, and Aboriginal heritage who shaped the town's unique multi-cultural architecture, and Jimmy Chi (acclaimed Aboriginal playwright).
stats.vibe: Highly relaxed, tropical, and multi-cultural. Life revolves around catching the sunset via iconic camel rides on Cable Beach or witnessing the "Staircase to the Moon"—a natural optical illusion caused by the full moon reflecting off exposed mudflats. The local culture is deeply tied to indigenous Yawuru heritage and historic Chinatown architecture.

timeline.text: Founded officially as a strategic pearling port, named after the colony's Governor, Sir Frederick Broome.
A submarine telegraph cable is laid from Broome to Indonesia, linking Australia directly to England for the first time.
Targeted by a devastating Axis air raid during World War World II, destroying flying boats hidden in the bay; wrecks are still visible at low tide today.

name: Busan
currencyLanguage: KRW (credit cards widely accepted; T-money card/cash useful for transit and street markets); Korean (English signage on metro/major sights).
gettingAshore: Most large cruise ships dock at the Busan International Cruise Terminal on Yeongdo Island (15–20 minute taxi or cruise shuttle across the bridge to Nampo-dong/Jagalchi) or at the Busan Port International Passenger Terminal in Jung-gu (10-minute walk to Busan Station/KTX and Metro Line 1). Confirm per call: Yeongdo vs. Jung-gu terminal, shuttle drop-off at Lotte Department Store/Nampo-dong, and Haedong Yonggungsa traffic times.

attractions.name: Jagalchi Fish Market, BIFF Square & Yongdusan Park (Busan Tower)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 15–20 min taxi/shuttle from Yeongdo terminal (or 10 min Metro Line 1 from Busan Station).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (flat bustling market lanes; escalators up to Yongdusan Park).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Low (indoor seafood halls and covered market arcades).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: South Korea's largest seafood market, teeming with live tanks and upstairs grilling restaurants, paired with lively street-food alleys and panoramic harbour views from Busan Tower.

attractions.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
attractions.tier: Local Transit / Independent or Guided Excursion

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 20–25 min taxi from cruise terminals (or Metro to Toseong + local green minibus).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Strenuous (very steep hillside alleys, narrow stairways, and uneven slopes).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate (exposed hillside neighbourhood).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Known as the "Machu Picchu of Busan," this hillside labyrinth of pastel-painted houses, murals, and artisan cafes overlooks Busan's working harbour.

attractions.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Seaside Temple & Haeundae Beach
attractions.tier: Local Transit / Independent or Guided Excursion

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 45–60 min drive northeast via Gwangan Bridge (allow buffer for heavy coastal traffic).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate (108 stone steps down to the coastal temple; flat beachfront promenade at Haeundae).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate-High (exposed rocky ocean cliffs).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Borderline (allow 4.5–5 hours due to cross-city traffic).

attractions.why: A rare 14th-century Buddhist temple perched directly on dramatic seaside rocks above crashing waves, combined with Busan's famous crescent sand beach.

attractions.name: Beomeosa Mountain Temple & UN Memorial Cemetery

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 30–45 min drive north/east depending on site.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate (stone temple courtyards and steps; flat manicured memorial parklands).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate.

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (allow 5–6 hours to combine both).

attractions.why: Contrasts a tranquil 1,300-year-old forested Silla-dynasty temple complex on Mount Geumjeongsan with the world's only UN-designated cemetery honouring Korean War soldiers.

shortDescription: South Korea's dynamic second-largest city and premier seaport, celebrated for colourful hillside Gamcheon Culture Village, cliffside Haedong Yonggungsa Temple, Jagalchi Fish Market, and Haeundae Beach.
longDescription: Stretching between rugged coastal mountains and the East Sea, Busan blends ultra-modern waterfront skyscrapers with historic Buddhist temples and bustling street-food markets. Depending on their berth, travelers can explore the pastel-painted terraced alleys of Gamcheon Culture Village, sample live-tank seafood at sprawling Jagalchi Fish Market, browse Gukje Market and BIFF Square, or visit Haedong Yonggungsa—a rare seaside Buddhist temple perched dramatically above crashing ocean waves near Haeundae's sandy shoreline.

tips.title: Know Your Cruise Terminal (Busan Port International vs. Yeongdo)
tips.text: Most ships dock at Busan Port International Passenger Terminal (BPIPT) beside Busan KTX Station (connected via pedestrian skybridge to metro/rail), while some vessels berth across the bridge at Yeongdo International Cruise Terminal (~15 minutes by shuttle/taxi to Nampo-dong and Jagalchi Market).

tips.title: T-money Transit Card & Map Apps
tips.text: Purchase and load a T-money card with South Korean Won (KRW) cash at any convenience store (CU, GS25, 7-Eleven) for seamless subway and bus rides; note that Google Maps walking/transit routing is restricted in South Korea—download Naver Map or KakaoMap (both offer English interfaces) before arriving.

tips.title: Traffic & Distance to Haedong Yonggungsa
tips.text: Located on Busan's northeastern coast, Haedong Yonggungsa Temple lies ~45–60 minutes from the port depending on heavy urban tunnel traffic—leave generous return cushion if taking a taxi independently.

tips.title: Hills & Stairs at Gamcheon Culture Village
tips.text: Gamcheon is built steeply into a mountainside with narrow stairways—take a taxi directly to the top entrance gate and walk downhill through the village before catching a taxi back from the bottom.

stats.intro: Busan is South Korea’s explosive, colorful maritime metropolis—a dynamic city that effortlessly pairs soaring neon skyscrapers and cutting-edge tech districts with historic cliffside Buddhist temples and sprawling urban beaches.
stats.neighbours: Gyeongju (the ancient "Museum Without Walls" capital of the historic Silla Kingdom, 35 minutes north via high-speed bullet train), Gamcheon Culture Village (a vibrant, kaleidoscopic hillside arts district located directly within the city limits).
stats.safety: Exceptionally safe and meticulously monitored by a comprehensive public CCTV and safety network. Street crime is negligible. Standard, casual big-city travel awareness is completely adequate.
stats.government: Highly stable, modern democratic metropolitan government within the Republic of Korea.
stats.economy: A multi-billion-dollar global trade juggernaut. Busan operates the world's sixth-busiest container cargo shipping port, supplemented by advanced automotive engineering, chemical manufacturing, digital media design, and international maritime tourism.
stats.famousPeople: Jungkook and Jimin (global music superstars of the pop phenomenon BTS), Actor Gong Yoo (star of Train to Busan and Squid Game).
stats.vibe: Fast-paced, ocean-loving, and intensely culinary. The city is famous for Haeundae Beach and the roaring Jagalchi Fish Market—the largest seafood market in the nation. It is also home to the breathtaking Haedong Yonggungsa Temple, one of the few Buddhist temples in Korea built directly on a craggy ocean cliff.

timeline.text: Designated by the Joseon Dynasty as the primary, high-volume international trading port linking commerce directly with Japan.
During the Korean War, Busan serves as the vital, heroic "Busan Perimeter" temporary capital—one of the only regions never conquered by North Korean forces.
The city hosts the landmark APEC Summit, unveiling the futuristic marine city skyscrapers and cementing its status as a top-tier global hub.

name: Cádiz
currencyLanguage: EUR; Spanish.
gettingAshore: Cruise ships berth at Muelle Alfonso XIII or Muelle Marqués de Comillas, directly bordering the historic old town. Passengers can step off the gangway and reach Plaza de San Juan de Dios and the historic core within a 5–10 minute flat walk. Confirm per call: pier berth, colour-coded walking lines on pavement, and Seville road/rail transfer times.

attractions.name: Cádiz Cathedral & Torre Tavira (Camera Obscura)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 10–15 min flat walk from pier.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (cathedral is accessible; Torre Tavira has 173 steps and no lift).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Low-Moderate.

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Explores Cádiz's golden-domed 18th-century cathedral alongside the city's highest historic watchtower, which projects live 360-degree panoramic views via a dark-room lens.

attractions.name: Roman Theatre of Cádiz (Teatro Romano)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 10 min flat walk from pier.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (modern interpretation centre with ramps; some ancient stone steps).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Low.

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Discovered accidentally in 1980 beneath the medieval El Pópulo neighbourhood, this 1st-century BC theatre is one of the oldest and largest in Roman Hispania.

attractions.name: Mercado Central de Abastos & La Caleta Beach

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 15 min walk to market; 25 min walk across peninsula to La Caleta.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (flat peninsula streets; sandy beach).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate (open-air central market stalls).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Sample fresh fried pescaíto, Iberian jamón, and local sherry at Spain's oldest covered municipal market before strolling to a picturesque beach flanked by two sea castles.

attractions.name: Jerez de la Frontera (Sherry Bodegas & Royal Equestrian School)
attractions.tier: Local Transit / Independent or Guided Excursion

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 35–40 min drive or direct Renfe commuter train (C-1) from Cádiz station.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (flat bodega cellars and arena seating).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: None (indoor equestrian show and cellar tours).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (allow 5–6 hours).

attractions.why: Tour historic cathedral-like sherry aging cellars and watch the famous How the Andalusian Horses Dance equestrian ballet in the birthplace of sherry wine.

links.label: Royal Andalusian School of Equestrian Art

attractions.name: Seville (Alcázar, Cathedral & Plaza de España)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 90 min drive each way via AP-4 highway.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Moderate-Strenuous (extensive walking over cobbles and palace courtyards).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (Seville regularly exceeds 35°C/95°F in summer).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (strictly an 8+ hour full-day excursion).

attractions.why: Andalusia's vibrant capital showcases Mudéjar royal palaces, the world's largest Gothic cathedral, and grand Renaissance pavilions.

shortDescription: Western Europe's oldest continuously inhabited city, set on a narrow sun-drenched peninsula where ships dock steps from golden-domed cathedrals, Roman ruins, sherry bodegas, and gateway access to Seville.
longDescription: Surrounded almost entirely by the Atlantic Ocean, Cádiz enchants cruise travelers with over 3,000 years of Phoenician, Roman, and Spanish maritime history packed onto a compact, flat, eminently walkable peninsula. Passengers step off the gangway directly into the historic centre, where colour-coded painted walking lines guide visitors to the golden-domed Cádiz Cathedral, the 1st-century BC Roman Theatre, the camera obscura atop Torre Tavira, and Spain's oldest covered municipal food market. Beyond the city's sea walls, regional trains and coaches connect easily to Jerez de la Frontera's historic sherry cellars and Andalusian equestrian ballet, or inland to the Mudéjar palaces of Seville.

tips.title: Follow the Painted Pavement Lines
tips.text: Cádiz makes independent exploration effortless—look just outside the Muelle Alfonso XIII / Marqués de Comillas port gates for four colour-coded walking trails painted directly on the sidewalks leading to major landmarks.

tips.title: Seville Requires a Full-Day Call
tips.text: Seville lies 90 minutes inland each way via the AP-4 highway; allow at least 8 hours in port and book a ship-sponsored excursion or early express train if visiting the Real Alcázar and Seville Cathedral.

tips.title: Torre Tavira Tickets
tips.text: The camera obscura live 360-degree projection at Torre Tavira admits small groups on timed schedules and involves climbing 173 steps (no elevator)—reserve a morning slot online if interested.

tips.title: Summer Heat & Siesta
tips.text: Andalusia regularly exceeds 35°C (95°F) in summer; explore open-air plazas early and sample fried pescaíto and local Manzanilla sherry at Mercado Central de Abastos around lunchtime.

stats.neighbours: Jerez de la Frontera (world capital of Sherry wine and Andalusian horses, 35 minutes north), Seville (capital of Andalusia, 1.5 hours north via high-speed train).
stats.safety: Exceptionally safe, warm, and highly walkable. The grid-like historic center is safe to explore at all hours.
stats.government: Highly stable municipality within the autonomous community of Andalusia, Spain.
stats.economy: Fueled by maritime ship repair yards, commercial shipping docks, fishing, and a highly robust summer cruise tourism industry.
stats.famousPeople: Manuel de Falla (celebrated classical composer), and Camarón de la Isla (legendary flamenco singer who trained extensively in the region).
stats.vibe: Famous for its grand baroque cathedral with its golden dome, a sprawling labyrinth of watchtowers used by 18th-century merchants, and its sharp, satirical Carnival festival.

timeline.text: Founded by Phoenician mariners as Gadir, establishing it as a crucial trading outpost beyond the Pillars of Hercules.
Sir Francis Drake launches a preemptive strike on the Spanish fleet in Cádiz harbor, famously called "singeing the King of Spain's beard."
The first liberal constitution of Spain (La Pepa) is written and declared within the besieged city walls.

name: Cairns
area: Australia — Queensland (Tropical North Queensland; gateway to Great Barrier Reef & Daintree Rainforest).
currencyLanguage: AUD (contactless cards and mobile tap accepted virtually everywhere); English.

officialLinks.label: Ports North — Cairns Cruise Liner Terminal

gettingAshore: Cruise ships berth right in downtown Cairns at the heritage-listed Cairns Cruise Liner Terminal on Trinity Wharf—a flat 5-minute walk from the Reef Fleet Terminal (departure point for Great Barrier Reef catamarans), Cairns Esplanade Lagoon, and downtown shops. Confirm per call: Trinity Wharf berth, Reef Fleet Terminal boarding cut-off, and Kuranda Scenic Railway / Skyrail schedule.

attractions.name: Great Barrier Reef (Outer Reef Pontoon or Green Island)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 5 min flat walk from ship to Reef Fleet Terminal + 45 min fast catamaran to Green Island (or 90 min to Outer Reef pontoon).

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (seated catamaran, underwater observatory, semi-submersible, or optional snorkelling/diving).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: High (open Coral Sea swell; stinger suits recommended Nov–May).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Borderline for Green Island (4.5–5 hrs); No for Outer Reef (strictly 6.5–8 hrs).

attractions.why: Experiences the world's largest coral reef system right from Cairns, offering vibrant coral gardens, sea turtles, reef fish, and glass-bottom boat viewing.

links.label: Tropical North Queensland — Great Barrier Reef

attractions.name: Kuranda Scenic Railway & Skyrail Rainforest Cableway
attractions.tier: Full-Day / Guided Excursion or Independent Transfer

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 15 min walk/taxi to Cairns Railway Station + 1 hr 45 min historic mountain train up + 1 hr 15 min Skyrail gondola down + 20 min coach transfer.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (step-free gondola cabins, accessible boardwalks, and vintage rail carriages).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate (tropical rainforest canopy mist and lush mountain views).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: No (allow 5.5–7 hours for the full rail-and-cableway loop).

attractions.why: Combines a historic 1891 railway winding past Barron Gorge waterfalls with a soaring cable car gliding just metres above the UNESCO-listed Wet Tropics rainforest canopy.

attractions.name: Cairns Esplanade Lagoon, Cairns Aquarium & Night Markets

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 5–15 min flat waterfront walk directly from Cairns Cruise Liner Terminal.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (flat seaside boardwalks and air-conditioned aquarium).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Low-Moderate (indoor aquarium; sunny tropical Esplanade).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Yes.

attractions.why: Stroll Cairns' palm-lined waterfront boardwalk and saltwater swimming lagoon before exploring the region's only aquarium dedicated exclusively to Tropical North Queensland ecosystems.

attractions.name: Hartley's Crocodile Adventures (Palm Cove / Wangetti)

logistics.label: Travel
logistics.text: 40–45 min scenic coastal drive north along Captain Cook Highway each way.

logistics.label: Physical
logistics.text: Low (flat timber boardwalks and covered lagoon boat cruise).

logistics.label: Weather
logistics.text: Moderate (shaded melaleuca wetlands and tropical sun).

logistics.label: 4-Hr Call
logistics.text: Borderline (allow 4.5–5 hours round-trip).

attractions.why: Features an eco-certified wetlands boat cruise where massive saltwater crocodiles leap for food alongside cassowaries, koalas, and venomous snake shows.

shortDescription: Tropical North Queensland's premier adventure gateway, offering direct walk-off catamaran access to the Great Barrier Reef alongside scenic railway and Skyrail gondola journeys into Kuranda's ancient rainforest.
longDescription: Framed by lush rainforest-clad mountains and the Coral Sea, Cairns is the only place on Earth where two UNESCO World Heritage ecosystems—the Great Barrier Reef and the Wet Tropics Rainforest—meet side by side. Docking right at the Cairns Cruise Liner Terminal in the heart of town, travelers can board high-speed reef catamarans steps from the pier to snorkel coral cays and the outer reef, soar above jungle canopies aboard the Skyrail Rainforest Cableway to the mountain village of Kuranda, ride the historic Kuranda Scenic Railway past Barron Falls, or explore the Cairns Esplanade Lagoon.

tips.title: Prime Walk-Off Pier & Reef Marina Access
tips.text: Ships dock at the Cairns Cruise Liner Terminal (Trinity Wharf) right downtown—the Reef Fleet Terminal (departure point for Great Barrier Reef catamarans to Green Island, Fitzroy Island, and Outer Reef pontoons) is a flat 5- to 10-minute waterfront walk next door.

tips.title: Allow Full-Day Buffers for Outer Reef & Kuranda
tips.text: Outer Great Barrier Reef cruises and Kuranda Scenic Railway / Skyrail loops typically run 6 to 8 hours; book ship-sponsored excursions for Outer Reef trips so the ship waits if ocean swells delay your catamaran's return.

tips.title: Tropical Stinger Season & Crocodile Safety
tips.text: From November through May, marine stingers require wearing full-body Lycra stinger suits (provided by reef operators) when snorkeling, and swimming at mainland beaches outside netted enclosures is unsafe; never swim or wade in unmarked tropical creeks, estuaries, or mangroves due to saltwater crocodiles.

tips.title: Rainforest Humidity & Reef-Safe Sunscreen
tips.text: Pack lightweight quick-dry clothing, insect repellent for rainforest walks, and reef-safe mineral sunscreen.

stats.intro: Cairns is a vibrant, tropical paradise globally celebrated as the ultimate premier gateway to two of the world's greatest natural wonders: the Great Barrier Reef and the ancient Daintree Rainforest.
stats.neighbours: The Great Barrier Reef (the world's largest coral reef system, accessible via high-speed vessels straight from the harbor), The Daintree Rainforest (the oldest continuously surviving tropical rainforest on Earth, 2 hours north), Kuranda (a historic mountain rainforest village accessible via a panoramic scenic railway).
stats.safety: Very safe, welcoming, and built entirely for global travelers. The primary safety tip is strictly environmental: never swim in local rivers or beaches outside designated, net-protected enclosures due to seasonal marine stingers and wild saltwater crocodiles.
stats.government: Highly stable municipal governance within the state of Queensland.
stats.economy: Intensely driven by international reef and eco-tourism, tropical agriculture (sugar cane and bananas), marine engineering, and commercial fishing fleets.
stats.famousPeople: Legend-rich Indigenous Gimuy Walubara Yidinji elders, and international sports stars like rugby legend Nate Myles.
stats.vibe: Energetic, tropical, and laid-back. Because there is no natural swimming beach directly downtown, life centers on the massive Cairns Esplanade Lagoon—a beautiful, 4,800-square-meter saltwater swimming pool overlooking the ocean. The town features bustling night markets, fresh tropical fruit stalls, and outdoor waterfront dining.

timeline.text: Founded officially as a mining port to service the goldfields discovered further inland, named after Governor William Wellington Cairns.
Serves as a vital frontline air and naval logistics base for Allied forces fighting the high-stakes Battle of the Coral Sea during World War II.
The Great Barrier Reef is formally inscribed onto the UNESCO World Heritage list, launching Cairns into a global tourism powerhouse.

shortDescription: A sun-soaked 3,000-year-old Spanish naval port where cruise ships dock steps from an excavated Roman theatre, Carthaginian defensive walls, elegant Art Nouveau boulevards, and hilltop castle views.
longDescription: Tucked inside a deep, naturally sheltered Mediterranean harbour flanked by fortified hills, Cartagena offers one of Spain's most walkable and rewarding cruise calls. Passengers step off the gangway straight onto the palm-lined Alfonso XII promenade, just minutes from the remarkably preserved 1st-century BC Roman Theatre—discovered hidden beneath a medieval neighbourhood in 1988—and the Punic Wall dating back to Hannibal's Carthaginian era. Pedestrianized Calle Mayor showcases ornate early-20th-century Modernista buildings, lively tapas squares serving local caldero rice and asiático layered coffee, and a panoramic glass elevator up to Castillo de la Concepción.

tips.title: Effortless Walk-Off Access
tips.text: The Terminal de Cruceros sits right at the edge of the historic centre; you do not need a shuttle or taxi to reach the Roman Theatre, Calle Mayor, Naval Museum, or Castillo de la Concepción panoramic lift.

tips.title: Combined Heritage Pass (Cartagena Puerto de Culturas)
tips.text: If planning to visit multiple archaeological sites (Roman Theatre, Punic Wall, Roman Forum District, and Panoramic Lift), purchase the bundled Cartagena Puerto de Culturas pass at the first museum or visitor kiosk for substantial savings.

tips.title: Midday Siesta Closures
tips.text: While major museums and waterfront cafes stay open through the afternoon, smaller independent boutiques along Calle Mayor often close for siesta between roughly 2:00 PM and 5:00 PM.

tips.title: Summer Heat & Sun Exposure
tips.text: Cartagena sits in one of Spain's warmest, driest microclimates—bring a sun hat, sunglasses, and water when climbing castle ramparts or exploring open-air Roman ruins.

stats.vibe: The city operates as a literal open-air museum, seamlessly integrating modern shopping promenades with ancient Roman ruins.

timeline.text: Founded by Hasdrubal the Fair as Qart Hadasht, serving as the Carthaginian military headquarters on the Iberian Peninsula.
Captured by Roman general Scipio Africanus during the Second Punic War and renamed Carthago Nova.
Isaac Peral launches his revolutionary electric submarine, which is proudly preserved on the Cartagena waterfront today.

name: Casablanca

gettingAshore: Ships dock inside the large commercial Port of Casablanca (Môle des Agrumes or container/cruise berths). Walking out through the busy industrial port gates takes 20–30 minutes and is not recommended; use cruise shuttles, official red petits taxis (negotiate fare or insist on meter), or pre-booked guides. Confirm per call: pier berth, port shuttle drop-off point, and Hassan II Mosque non-Muslim guided tour times (closed during prayer times).
